utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Chuqing, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you follow in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I can. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Please take a chair. Appearances, Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Ann Sutherland, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning to you both. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. David Cunningham with Aleksandar Vujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you both. Do you have any preliminaries on your part? No. Yesterday -- Ms. Sutherland, I know that you're probably going to be caught -- taken unaware on this, but yesterday when Ms. Korner was here and Mr. Ackerman was here, we discussed very briefly an oral motion that Ms. Korner made or presented, to admit or to have admitted, under Rule 92 bis, statements by alleged rape victims in Kotor Varos. Mr. Ackerman did respond yesterday, along the lines that, as far as the rape -- alleged rapes themselves and sexual crimes themselves are alleged, he was resorting to the previous practice, in other words, he would not raise any objection. However, with regard to other details, particularly, for example, the siege, later ethnic cleansing or whatever, then he reserved his position and the indication was that he would not be in favour of admitting those parts of the statements under Rule 92 bis. Position as we left it yesterday was that I would go through the statements, because I hadn't seen them as yet. I don't know if there is -- if you want to update me, either of you. I know it's not something that I discussed with you yesterday, but I don't know if you are in a position to update me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further information on that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, I don't have any information either, but I'll call Mr. Ackerman at the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you can. The position, as I see it, is -- and you also need to tell me -- you -- please sit down. You also need to tell me where, in case they are admitted under Rule 92 bis, whether we need to give them some protective measure. They -- I don't seem to have an application for the granting of protective measures. Or do you refer to them by BT number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If my memory serves me correctly, they were included in the motion that we filed for all the municipalities on the 26th of June, 2002, and they were granted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Pseudonym. Certainly pseudonym and image distortion, if not closed session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see. All right. Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If they want to testify in that regard on the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I didn't come across that. So that explains why they already have a BT number. With regard to the first witness, BT74, pages -- from the middle of page 1 to practically page 5. There are events which -- page 6, actually. There are events that do not relate to rape but relate to other events, other events anyway, but including burning of some people in a barn and how the whole lot were then moved to the sawmill. Then from page -- rape is only page -- practically part of page 6, the whole of page 7 and part of page 8. And then the rest of page 8 is about ethnic cleansing. I think you need to direct me there, particularly on the part of the Defence, because we need to take a decision pretty soon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps if Mr. Ackerman can provide the statements to the Prosecution with the parts that he wishes to be redacted, then we can go from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Supposedly I think that's how it was put yesterday, or how it was suggested by Ms. Korner. So if that could be done, Mr. Cunningham, over -- in the course of today, it would be preferred, because then I can decide in the course of the day. If it cannot be done today, please, Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I'll try to get it done today, Judge. I have a sinking feeling it will probably be Monday. Both of those witnesses with regard to the sexual assaults in Kotor Varos were going to be my witnesses, so I'm the one that's more knowledgeable about the statements, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. But anyway, I'm raising the matter. The second statement is again not as perhaps controversial as the first one, but you do have the first two and a half, three pages dealing with other matters and not sexual crimes or gender-related crimes. So next witness is closed session, if I remember well now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's bring the curtains town. My apologies to the members of the public. This is a very sensitive witness and we need to hear the evidence in closed session. Now, before the witness comes in, Mr. Cunningham, how long do you think you need -- how much time do you need for your cross, things being what they are now?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: My guess is an hour. I've talked to Ms. Sutherland about that already this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. You have discussed it amongst yourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's how I want it to be done between now and the end. Just try to organise yourselves and give and take and we can move ahead. So you know where you stand. You need to allow the entire last session for Mr. Cunningham, and maybe between 15 to 30 minutes of the second. All right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 30th day of June, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.54 p.m.,
